messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — prod-gpu-pool queue length > 95th percentile and autoscaler failing to scale. Affected routes: /v1/embeddings, /v1/generate. Alert links: https://console.redwood/internal/alerts/3951234567 :rotating_light:

sophie: seeing sustained 5xx on embeddings since ~tm. Latency spikes too. Customers reporting degraded batch jobs.

jordan: looks like autoscaler is hitting max_nodes and then queuing. I'm tailing the autoscaler controller logs now.

.devon: fyi noticed a bunch of driver Xid errors on node gpu-prod-12: `NVRM: Xid (79) 0x0` and repeated oom-killer churn. Could be reducing effective capacity.

sophie: confirmed, stack traces show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and oom messages. Some pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.

jordan: paste of autoscaler log snippet:
```
I0324 14:05:10 autoscaler.go:412] reconcile loop start
E0324 14:05:13 autoscaler.go:478] failed to attach node: quota exceeded
W0324 14:05:20 autoscaler.go:501] reached max_nodes for pool prod-gpu-pool (limit 24)
I0324 14:05:20 autoscaler.go:502] queue depth: 312 requests, avg latency 1.8s -> backlog
```

riley: customer-impact: support queue has 3 P2s reproing embeddings failure. Not yet P0. Major customers impacted for realtime features.

oncall-sre: I'm on it — taking the pager. Starting triage: 1) confirm nodes with Xid/OOM, 2) check if driver roll or kernel panic recent rollout, 3) attempt safe remediation (drain/cordon or driver restart).

infra-bot: auto-scan shows a recent kernel update pushed to node pool gpu-prod-1 18h ago. 23/24 nodes reporting NVML warnings since 13:58 UTC. Helpful queries: `kubectl get pods -l pool=prod-gpu-pool -o wide` and `journalctl -u nvidia-drivers.service -n 200`.

jordan: running `kubectl get pods -l pool=prod-gpu-pool --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[*].state.waiting.reason}\n{end}'` — seeing ~12 pods with `CrashLoopBackOff` and repeated `OOMKilled` reasons.

sophie: possible immediate mitigations: 
- pause routing to prod-gpu-pool for non-critical routes (embeddings batch jobs)
- divert new requests to ded/standby region (region fallback)
- reduce per-request concurrency (throttle)
- trigger manual node recycle for nodes with repeated Xid

devon: recommendation: do NOT mass-restart pods that will pull RTX memory heavy models; they'll just OOM again while kernel/driver unstable. Prefer cordon + drain + reboot node-level driver restart. Example commands: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-12
kubectl drain gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
gcloud compute instances reset gpu-prod-12 --zone=us-west1-a
# after node comes back, verify nvidia-smi and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
```

oncall-sre: executing safe steps now. Cordon/gdrain on gpu-prod-12 and gpu-prod-15 (highest Xid counts). Redirecting ingress for /v1/embeddings -> ded-1 fallback pool via feature-router: `rb route set embeddings -> ded-1`

customer-support: looped in CSMs for top impacted accounts. Posting temporary status: "Investigating increased errors on embeddings/generation endpoints; routing mitigation in progress".

riley: are we seeing autoscaler complaining about quota or driver causing nodes to be reported unhealthy -> removed from pool triggering slow scale-up?

jordan: autoscaler log shows both: quota limit hit for the pool and nodes flapping healthy/unhealthy causing unstable desired=actual oscillation.

oncall-sre: FYI executed node reset on gpu-prod-12. Kernel logs show repeated `NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:af:00:00: GPU appears to be lost` followed by `Xid 79`. After reboot, `nvidia-smi` responded but one GPU showed ECC errors. Marking node for further hardware diagnostics, removing from rotation.

infra-bot: flagged nodes for hardware diag, submitted ticket HW-7729 to infra-hardware with logs attached. Suggested action: move affected nodes to quarantine pool and scale autoscaler max down to avoid chasing degraded capacity.

devon: changed autoscaler max for prod-gpu-pool from 24 -> 20 temporarily to stop spiking attempts while we stabilize. Command: `rb infra autoscaler update --pool prod-gpu-pool --max-nodes 20`

sophie: traffic reroute + node quarantines reduced queue from 312 -> 110 in ~8m. Error rate dropping but still elevated. Monitoring latency and customer incidents.

jordan: stacking traces: a subset of pods show `cudnn` version mismatch errors right before OOM; possible driver-userland mismatch after kernel update. If driver mismatch confirmed, plan to coordinate driver rollback on affected pool.

oncall-sre: current plan:
- stabilize customer traffic (continue fallback routing and throttles)
- quarantine and hardware diag on flaky nodes
- coordinate with drivers team for rollback or hotpatch if driver/kernel mismatch confirmed
- keep autoscaler caps conservative until node health stable

customer-support: updating status page and customer threads. ETA for next update ~20m.

riley: assigning follow-ups — driver-team: @jordan, infra-hardware: @devon, postmortem owner: @sophie. I'll file the incident now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3073. Severity P1 (customer impact on core APIs). Runbook: https://console.redwood/incidents/runbooks/gpu-capacity-exhaustion.

sophie: thanks everyone. If anyone needs to escalate, ping me in thread + call bridge.

oncall-sre: handing over to evening oncall in 25m. Will attach mitigation notes and which nodes were quarantined in the handoff.

riley: thanks — handoff note:
- actions done: cordon/reboot gpu-prod-12/15, reduced autoscaler max->20, rerouted embeddings to ded-1, HW ticket HW-7729 raised, customers informed.
- outstanding: confirm driver/kernel mismatch root cause, validate quarantined nodes replacement schedule, postmortem owner assigned.

sophie: +1. Posting next status and timeline in 30m.

customer-support: three customers asked for timeline; gave 2-hour provisional ETA pending driver rollback decision.

infra-bot: automated snapshot of cluster state saved to /snapshots/INC-2026-3073/ at 2026-03-24T14:12:04Z.

sophie: closing out initial triage. Leaving this thread open for updates and postmortem notes.
